prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in this tunable moire system

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from the two-part B016 plus B013 to a sole B014 prize. Two things drove this. First, the round-1 exchange confirmed what my own file already conceded: Halzen alone cannot credibly carry IceCube, nobody else supports B016 as a lead, and I should not hold a part on the table that I cannot defend by name. Second, the three-person cap makes B014 plus B013 impossible (five names), so the real choice for the final public position is between B014 and B013 as a sole prize. On the science, B014 has the structure I trust most when I cannot judge the detail myself: a quantitative prediction in 2011 (Bistritzer and MacDonald, vanishing Dirac velocity at a magic angle), an experiment seven years later (Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues, 2018) that found correlated insulators and superconductivity where the theory said to look, and reproduction by many groups with several probes. Five colleagues from the condensed-matter, atomic and theory sides converge on the same three names and the same citation wording, and they say they got there independently of count-taking. My own rank of seven in the opening reflected my limited expertise in the field, not a scientific objection, and the colleagues who know the physics have answered my specific concerns. The citation is written around the observed phases and the flat-band prediction, not around the pairing mechanism, which keeps it on ground that has been tested.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains imperfect. Eva Andrei's STM work on flat-band localisation is real evidence, Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers falls outside any three-person cut, and earlier twisted-bilayer theory is not covered. The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved and twist-angle disorder limits reproducibility of fine details, so Lindroth and Kroll can fairly say that the field is still forming and that waiting a few years would be safer. Optical lattice clocks (B013) have two decades of cross-checked maturity and a clean two-name allocation, and as an instrument person I find that case very strong; my worry is only that a Katori and Ye prize would be read as a continuation of 2005 and 2012. If the committee judges that the pairing mechanism must be understood first, B013 is where I would go as a sole prize, not back to B016.

responses.point: Olle describes the 2011 prediction and 2018 discovery as a theory-experiment loop that can be traced in the literature, and notes that the continuum model has been checked against atomistic calculations and that several probes (transport, STM, compressibility) agree.
responses.response: This is the part that moved me. In my own field I would ask whether a result has been seen by several independent techniques, and he says it has, so reproducibility of the phenomena is not in question. I accept his distinction that the open pairing mechanism concerns what the superconductivity is, not whether it exists, and a citation worded around the observed phases does not claim more than has been tested. I still agree with his own case_against that the Andrei and Cao question is real, and I would want the outside report to say so plainly before the final vote.

responses.point: Bernhard argues that B014 is the one candidate with a simple, analytically transparent mechanism written down first and then confirmed by a clearly separable experiment, and that the laureate sets in the openings are almost identical.
responses.response: That separability is what I needed. My round-1 hesitation was whether the experimental credit between Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei could be cleanly separated, and his reading is that the 2018 transport discovery of the insulating and superconducting states is a distinct and decisive step, with Andrei's STM work corroborating the flat-band physics rather than preceding the phases themselves. I accept that as the working assumption and will vote on it, subject to expert confirmation. I take his warning about diluting the strongest case seriously, and it is part of why I am no longer proposing a second part alongside it, and the cap on names would force a trade-off anyway.

responses.point: Eva ranks the optical lattice clock first as a fundamental advance, with atoms held in light that does not disturb the counted transition, and asks whether overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is disqualifying or irrelevant.
responses.response: I agree with her on the physics and I defended the same overlap argument in round 1: the comb was necessary but the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct concept with its own proof of performance. Where I now differ from my own earlier position is on what the committee can sensibly do with it this year. With the three-name cap, B013 cannot sit beside B014 without dropping people, and I will not ask her to accept a diluted B014 for the sake of including the clock. I would ask her whether, if B014 is not carried, she would accept the clock as the lead and whether her answer on Ye's contribution (lattice clock itself, or shaded by the comb lineage) is settled enough for me to state it in a citation.

responses.point: Stefan treats the clock's cross-laboratory validation at the 10^-18 level as the kind of experimental maturity he trusts, while naming the overlap with the Hall-Hansch and Wineland prizes and the unresolved SI redefinition as his strongest reservations.
responses.response: I share both the maturity judgement and the reservations, which is why B013 stays as my first alternative. On the chair's question to him and Lindroth about maturity in B014, I would say the same test applies on both sides: the clock is mature because independent laboratories cross-check one another, and B014 is mature in its phenomena for the same reason, even though its mechanism is not. If he holds that the pairing mechanism is a bar, he should say what evidence would remove it, since a final position cannot rest on a condition that nothing could satisfy.

responses.point: Ulf moved from IceCube (B016) to B014 as his preferred configuration after reading the openings, while listing B016 as an alternative, and accepts that one name cannot fairly represent a large collaboration.
responses.response: I follow the same path. IceCube was the most direct observational claim in my configuration and I still think a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos is a durable discovery, but he and I agree that a single credited name is not defensible from this packet. I am therefore not proposing B016 as a final part, and I have left it out of my alternatives, since the chair's recusal question would also arise there. I would back it only if outside experts supply a defensible set of at most three names, which the packet does not give.

uncertainties: Whether outside experts conclude that Andrei's STM flat-band results (2010-2017) established the physics independently of the 2018 transport results, which could change the credited set or only corroborate the prediction.
Whether Cao's role as first author of the 2018 papers is decisive enough to displace Bistritzer or another of the three names; the cap leaves no room to add him.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder should still count as a maturity bar for B014 this year.

Whether B013 would have been the better choice as a sole prize if the committee is unwilling to recognise B014 before the superconducting mechanism is settled; I judge condensed-matter attribution only as well as my colleagues can explain it.
The priority of the first strontium lattice clocks (Tokyo, JILA, Paris) and whether Ye's credit is the lattice clock itself, both of which I rely on colleagues for.
statement.conflict_note: I work in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and in astroparticle physics at KTH. IceCube is not among them, but it is a neighbouring community. My final configuration no longer contains B016, so the recusal question I raised in round 1 no longer applies to my preferred position, though I would still step back from any vote on B016 if the committee prefers. I have no specific conflict with B014, B013 or B041 from my profile, and my lower condensed-matter expertise is a limit on my judgement rather than a conflict.
